paradoxes.text: Luttwak's thesis in the data: the rise summons the coalition. A state that grows economically, militarily and politically at once provokes the reaction that the logic of strategy predicts, and 'great-state autism' keeps it from seeing the reaction as its own work. Japan's 'greatest strategic challenge' (Aug 2026), fourteen states on the 2016 award (Jul 2026), AUKUS, the Quad, 'systemic rival', the security services of Tallinn, Riga, Oslo and Stockholm, a Philippine president who invites the US back: each is a weight added to the other scale by Beijing's own hand.

paradoxes.text: Beijing has learned the lesson where it costs least and unlearned it where it costs most. The thaws of 2025-26 - India at Tianjin and Delhi, Australia's A$20bn of restrictions lifted, Lee in Beijing, Starmer in Beijing, To Lam's visit, the EU's ten-point list, three truces with Trump - are a state deliberately lowering its weight on the scale. grand_strategy.reading:
China in October 2026 is the case Luttwak wrote the book about, read from the inside.
At the technical level the instruments are the best in the world and growing: the
largest navy by hulls, a third carrier, a coast guard with a licence to fire, a
monopoly on the magnets everyone's motors need, a trade surplus of USD 1.2 trillion.
At the level of theatre strategy the record is mixed by design: the Taiwan Strait is
rehearsed twice a year and never crossed, the shoals are taken by water cannon and
nature reserves rather than by landings, the Senkakus are visited 357 days a year.
At the level of grand strategy the paradox Luttwak predicted is visible in every
file of this atlas: Japan calls China its greatest challenge, fourteen states
reaffirm an award Beijing calls null, the EU keeps 'systemic rival', and the one
rival that matters, the United States, had to be bought into three truces with the
rare-earth lever that each truce spends. What is new in 2025-26 is that Beijing
appears to have read the logic: the thaws with India, Australia, South Korea,
Britain, Vietnam and even Brussels are a great state lowering its weight on the
scale, and the handling of Trump - hospitality, soybeans, a Board of Trade, 'healthy
competition kept within bounds' - is relational manoeuvre of a high order. What is
old is the reflex: one sentence from Takaichi brought back the whole arsenal of
coercion against the neighbour whose rearmament costs China most, and the
Philippine shoals got batons in the same summer. The constraints are heavier than
the rhetoric admits - deflation, 7.9 million births, a purged high command, a strait
it does not control and a chip embargo it cannot answer in kind - and they are why
the squeeze stays short of war. Three signals that are not rows: Beijing has let the
Power of Siberia 2 price wait for over a year, the measure of who is senior; it
asked Tehran, not Washington, to reopen Hormuz; and it made its best offer to Trump
on Taiwan not with a threat but with a request. The question the card leaves open
is Luttwak's own: whether a state can keep learning the logic of strategy faster
than its own weight teaches the others.

stances.note: Rival, the atlas's reference case for the grade (ONTOLOGY: 'the US toward China'), read here from Beijing: competition over technology, trade, Taiwan and the order, no will to destroy the other. Beijing's own words are 'healthy competition kept within bounds' and no 'Thucydides trap' (Xi, Washington, 24 Sep 2026); its structure is a chip embargo it cannot answer in kind, an 'affiliates rule' and a 47% tariff wall answered with rare-earth licences and the market. Warming because three summits in eleven months (Busan 30 Oct 2025, Beijing 14-16 May 2026, Washington 23-25 Sep 2026) each extended the truce, launched a Board of Trade and an AI dialogue, cut tariffs on about USD 30bn of goods and put military-to-military channels back; Brookings reads Xi as preferring 'anemic stability to no stability at all'. Not partner: the truce is a pause on each side's weapons (soybeans excluded, magnets 20% below trend, the arms package to Taiwan 'in abeyance' but not withdrawn), not an alignment. Bond - grievance: the Taiwan Relations Act and arms sales since 1979, the 1999 Belgrade embassy bombing and the 'containment' narrative are the standing wound in Beijing's reading, whatever the mood of the summit.

The squeeze is the method: Strait Thunder (Apr 2025) and Justice Mission (29-31 Dec 2025, the closest live fire so far, a Type 075 for the first time), the 'diehard' list (14 names and 12 accomplices by 7 Jan 2026, death penalty in absentia under the June 2024 guidelines), cable incidents, and the KMT received by Xi (10 Apr 2026) while the DPP government is refused. Stable, not cooling: air sorties in 2026 are about half of 2025 and no named exercise followed the two Trump summits, because the American channel is now the main instrument - Xi asked Trump in Washington to 'oppose' independence and the second arms package sits 'in abeyance'. Bond - kin: 'one family', the civil war, language; a feud in the atlas's terms.

stances_toward.note: Our reading of the structure, not a label any source uses (the brief for this card suggested 'partner'; the structural rule of ONTOLOGY.md points the other way and the reviewer should decide). For: China takes almost a third of Australia's trade; Albanese was in Beijing on 12-18 Jul 2025 for the Annual Leaders' Meeting with Li Qiang, after Beijing had removed the trade barriers that cost Australian exporters more than A$20bn a year; no source records a stated aim of defeating China. Against 'partner': AUKUS, the Quad and the whole Pacific treaty web (vetoes on third-party security in the Nauru and Tuvalu treaties, a ban on foreign bases in the Vanuatu agreement, a treaty bid for Solomon Islands against the 2022 China policing pact) are built to deny Beijing a foothold; the PLA Navy's live-fire exercise in the Tasman Sea (21-22 Feb 2025, 49 flights diverted) was a show of reach; Albanese reasserted in January 2026 the election pledge to return Port Darwin to Australian control, and Ambassador Xiao Qian warned that Beijing would feel obliged to take measures to protect the Chinese company's legitimate interests. The Diplomat's 2024 phrase 'frenemies' sums the mix. Warming because the leader-level thaw since 2022 has outrun the structural hedge, and the trade is flowing. Not adversary: the aim is deterrence and denial, not Beijing's defeat. Bond - none: pure interest.
